record.original_question: Does there exist a holomorphic map F : P^k → P^k with a T wandering Fatou component U, i.e. F n (U) F m (U) = ∅ for all n 6= m?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.3.4 Does there exist a holomorphic map F : Pk → Pk with a T wandering Fatou component U, i.e. F n (U) F m (U) = ∅ for all n 6= m?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k \geq 2$ and let $\mathbb{P}^k = \mathbb{P}^k(\mathbb{C})$ denote complex projective space. A holomorphic map $F: \mathbb{P}^k \to \mathbb{P}^k$ has Fatou set $\mathcal{F}(F)$ equal to the largest open subset of $\mathbb{P}^k$ on which the family of iterates $\{F^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ is normal (locally equicontinuous). A connected component $U$ of $\mathcal{F}(F)$ is called a wandering Fatou component if $F^n(U) \cap F^m(U) = \emptyset$ for all integers $n \neq m \geq 0$ (equivalently, no component containing $F^n(U)$ ever coincides with one containing $F^m(U)$).

Question: Does there exist a holomorphic endomorphism $F: \mathbb{P}^k \to \mathbb{P}^k$ (for some $k \geq 2$) admitting a wandering Fatou component?
artifact.status_search_result: Astorg, Buff, Dujardin, Peters, and Raissy (Annals of Mathematics, 2016) constructed polynomial skew-product endomorphisms of $\mathbb{C}^2$ that extend holomorphically to $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ and possess a wandering Fatou component, answering the question affirmatively for $k=2$ (and hence for all $k\geq 2$). The construction uses parabolic implosion techniques.

status_evidence.title: A two-dimensional polynomial mapping with a wandering Fatou component
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial skew-products of C^2 possessing a wandering Fatou component; these mappings extend holomorphically to P^2(C).
status_evidence.claim: Provides a holomorphic endomorphism of P^2 with a wandering Fatou component.

status_evidence.title: Annals of Mathematics, vol. 184 (2016)
